objections.gloss: The objection makes no claim about what grounds the privilege. It is a flank — the move the anthropocentrist turns to once the ground-lattice has bottomed out and only a standoff of permissions…
objections.title: > "Set every argument aside. What actually moves you to deny humanity any special standing is not the weakness of the grounds — it is animus: contempt for your own kind, dressed in the language of unproven mandates and absent capacities. A stance powered by hatred of humanity is not one you are *permitted* to hold as a serious moral position; it is self-harm in the costume of philosophy, and it disqualifies itself. Grant that every ground-argument failed — your dissent still stands convicted by its motive. You do not withhold because the case is thin; you withhold because you despise what you are, and you would not lift a finger to keep the species in the world. (Or, more gently: you do not really *lack* the human-intuition every human shares. You are posturing. Either way the refusal is not in good standing.)"

objections.gloss: The objection has metabolized the parity defeat and fallen back to the one position parity declined to settle. It grants that no capacity coincides with the species border, abandons the bright line…
objections.title: > "Concede the parity gap whole — I won't smuggle a threshold, and I won't draw the line at the species border, because you've shown no genuine capacity falls there. But you assumed I needed a line at all. Drop the threshold framing: standing is not a badge you clear a bar to wear, it is a *magnitude*, and the magnitude tracks capacity. Humans, on average, have more of what grounds standing — more rational agency, richer self-awareness, deeper temporal extension — and so, on average, more standing. The marginal cases stop being counterexamples and become confirmations: the profoundly impaired human has proportionally less, the exceptional animal proportionally more, exactly as a gradient predicts. I bite that without a wince. There is no line for you to break because I have drawn none — only a slope, and on the slope humans simply rank highest. The gradient is honest where the line was crude."

objections.gloss: The objection runs on one equivocation and one smuggled asymmetry. **The equivocation:** it treats *where belief begins* as *what belief is owed* — incumbency read as a justificatory credential.…
objections.title: Anthropocentrism is the **default**. It is woven into language (we say "person" and mean human; "humane" is a compliment), into law (rights attach to humans as such), into practice, and into pre-reflective intuition. A position that pervasive and that load-bearing does not stand in need of a defense — it *is* the resting state of reasoning about moral standing. The dissenter is the one making the **extraordinary claim**: that humanity's privileged standing should be revoked or suspended. Extraordinary claims carry the burden of proof. So the dissenter, not the anthropocentrist, owes an argument. And until that positive argument for de-privileging humanity is actually **discharged**, human-centrism stands as the *rational* default — and dissent from it, having produced no such argument, is **arbitrary, perverse, even irrational**: a departure from the settled with nothing to show for it.

objections.gloss: The grounded objection runs on one equivocation and one mid-argument substitution. **The equivocation:** *capacity-bearer* is read as *category-member* — "the bearers of C" slides into "the members…
objections.title: > "Concede the burden is symmetric — I won't lean on the default. Here is the ground. Humans possess capacity **C**: rational agency, the capacity to give and demand reasons, to enter reciprocal justification, to hold oneself answerable to norms — name it as you like, it is real and it is morally weighty. And the marginal cases don't embarrass it: a kind is characterized by its mature, typical form, not by its damaged exceptions. So the privilege is not arbitrary incumbency — it *tracks* C. Anthropocentrism is just the recognition that bearers of C are owed a standing the C-less are not, and humans are the bearers of C." This is the privilege the anti-mandate node (`human-centrism-is-the-default`) explicitly declined to engage and handed forward: the spine defeats the privilege only while it is *bare*; the moment a ground is named, the dispute moves here. The objection has pre-loaded its best defense (the kind-norm rescue) into the first statement. Good — it gets met.

objections.gloss: The deepest objection runs on a primitive wrapped in two recoverable errors. **The primitive (irrecoverable, and correctly so):** kind-membership-as-such, placed beyond justification (Williams). A…
objections.title: > "Concede parity — capacity doesn't carve at the species line; I won't rest the privilege on a trait some humans lack and some animals share. But you assumed the ground had to be a *capacity*. It needn't be. Membership in the human kind — the human form of life — is *itself* the morally relevant fact, not derivatively through any capacity. It is **the kind that matters** (Cohen); the marginal human has standing *qua* member. And the demand for a *species-neutral* justification of human partiality is confused (Williams): it asks me to occupy a 'point of view of the universe' from which the very notion of what-matters loses its grip. **'They're human, like us' is already a complete reason.** Calling it 'prejudice' begs the question — it assumes species is morally idle the way race is, which is precisely what's in dispute. There is nothing here for you to refute, and no neutral tribunal you can summon me to."

objections.gloss: The objection runs on the same primitive as brute-kind, dressed as matter rather than membership — but it carries one over-reach brute-kind does not have, and that over-reach is where the distinct…
objections.title: > "Concede the capacity dialectic and concede the kind-membership dialectic both. I am not resting standing on a trait, and I am not resting it on abstract kind. I am resting it on what a thing is made of and as: a living, biological organism. Standing-bearing properties — a point of view, interests, the capacity to be wronged — can inhere only in that kind of substrate. A silicon system, however fluently it behaves, is the wrong sort of thing for them to inhere in. So the non-biological case is not a *member* whose standing I am denying. It is a category to which standing-talk does not reach — and your readiness to extend standing to it is not generosity, it is a category mistake."
